keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

keywords.name: Time-series foundation models
keywords.about: Unified time-series foundation models share representations and dynamics; forecasting benchmarks compare selectors.

keywords.name: On-policy distillation
keywords.about: On-policy distillation is made verifiable and compared with reinforcement learning for reasoning.

keywords.name: Coding agents
keywords.about: Coding and general agents are benchmarked for performance claims, skills, and defense failures.

keywords.name: Video generation
keywords.about: Video generators are conditioned on geometry, knowledge, and streaming memory for efficient synthesis.

keywords.name: World models
keywords.about: World models remember surprising video events and test whether occupancy dynamics follow actions.

keywords.name: World-action models
keywords.about: World-action models predict latent futures and scale with long context for manipulation.

keywords.name: Vision-language models
keywords.about: Vision-language models are probed for expert reliance, audio-visual grounding, and universal harnessing.

keywords.name: LLM judges
keywords.about: Language-model judges are audited for prompt-date bias, validation bias, and simulator assurance.

keywords.name: GUI agents
keywords.about: GUI agents synchronize action timing and use semantic probes for grounding and decoding.

keywords.name: FFN
keywords.about: Feed-forward layers and residual interfaces are reworked in transformer and encoder architectures.

keywords.name: 3D reconstruction
keywords.about: Structure-from-motion and Gaussian splatting recover camera poses from rotated and event views.

keywords.name: Bimanual dexterous manipulation
keywords.about: Bimanual hands learn dexterous manipulation from egocentric touch and fabric benchmarks.

keywords.name: Physical plausibility
keywords.about: Robot and video world models are tested for physically plausible contacts, motion, and rewards.

keywords.name: Diffusion models
keywords.about: Diffusion training improves posterior sampling, noise-level adjacency, and VAE anchoring.

themes.name: LLM agent security and reliability
themes.summary: Papers address security and reliability of language-model agents, covering prompt injection, shared-memory poisoning, recovery from failures, authorization, defenses, and evaluation harnesses. They differ in whether they attack agents, repair environments, or measure deployment risks.

themes.name: Vision-language-action robot manipulation
themes.summary: Papers study vision-language-action models for robot manipulation, covering corrections, spatial grounding, three-dimensional geometry, continual learning, bimanual and dexterous control, memory, and fabrication benchmarks. They differ in whether they improve policies, evaluate robustness, or analyze deployment safety.

themes.name: Diffusion and flow-matching generative modeling
themes.summary: Papers develop diffusion and flow-matching generative models, spanning joint representations, posterior sampling, noise-level training, VAE fine-tuning, video diffusion caching and attention, distillation, and manifold priors. They differ in whether they improve training, sampling, efficiency, or physical alignment.

themes.name: LLM benchmark validity and evaluation bias
themes.summary: Papers examine the validity and reliability of language-model benchmarks and evaluators, including validation bias, hidden prompt variables, persona effects, judge reliability, synthetic dialogue fidelity, and overspecified tests. They differ in whether they audit model responses, benchmark design, or scoring pipelines.

themes.name: Mechanistic interpretability and representation geometry
themes.summary: Papers probe internal mechanisms and representation geometry in transformers and multimodal models, using recurrence tasks, layer readouts, spectral analysis, expert lesions, functional networks, reward bases, and causal abstraction. They differ in whether they explain behavior, select layers, or diagnose hidden computation.

themes.name: Medical multimodal foundation models and segmentation
themes.summary: Papers develop medical multimodal foundation models and segmentation methods for pathology, proteomics, imaging, retrieval, clinical spatial reasoning, and surgical understanding. They differ in whether they build foundation models, benchmarks, calibration methods, or domain-specific pipelines.

themes.name: Speculative decoding and efficient LLM inference
themes.summary: Papers improve efficient language-model inference through speculative decoding, draft training, parallel drafting, KV-cache consolidation, quantization, pruning, hybrid attention, and GUI action decoding. They differ in whether they optimize acceptance, memory, hardware kernels, or application latency.

themes.name: 3D Gaussian splatting and reconstruction
themes.summary: Papers advance Gaussian splatting and reconstruction, covering sparse-view priors, four-dimensional tornado reconstruction, streaming SLAM, LiDAR simulation, hierarchical rendering, and hand-object meshes. They differ in whether they improve rendering speed, geometry, calibration, or scene assets.

themes.name: Embodied world-action models
themes.summary: Papers build embodied world-action models that predict future visual and geometric states together with actions, using multi-view generation, latent future prediction, long context, humanoid interaction, and physical plausibility benchmarks. They differ in whether they emphasize representation, scaling, control speed, or evaluation.

themes.name: Privacy attacks and model watermarking
themes.summary: Papers study privacy and integrity attacks and defenses for models, including query obfuscation, cross-session disclosure, fingerprinting, memorization auditing, adversarial image protection, watermarking, and bit-flip attacks. They differ in whether they expose vulnerabilities, design defenses, or audit ownership.

themes.name: Time-series foundation models and forecasting
themes.summary: Papers study time-series foundation models and forecasting, including leaderboard resolution, tokenization and architecture roles, multimodal selection, multiple input and output lengths, shared dynamics, and anomaly detection. They differ in whether they evaluate boards, design architectures, or handle missing sensors.

themes.name: On-policy distillation for LLM post-training

They differ in whether they transfer teacher feedback, combine reinforcement learning, or unify heterogeneous specialists.

highlights.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
highlights.authors: Guo Chen, Fuxiao Liu, Haoqin Tu et al.
highlights.why: Releases an agentic visual creation framework with a new tokenizer, 30B autoregressive image model, and vision-code models, improving PSNR and benchmark scores.
highlights.key_result: On approximately 178K images spanning six visual domains, our tokenizer improves reconstruction PSNR from 26.08 to 29.57 dB over Emu3.5 IBQ and provides 7.13 faster encoding and 10.93 faster decoding at batch size one on A100.

highlights.title: The Date You Didn't Set: The System-Prompt Date as a Hidden Variable in LLM Evaluation
highlights.authors: Noureldin Zahran, Mohammed E. Fouda, and Khaled N. Khasawneh
highlights.theme: LLM benchmark validity and evaluation bias
highlights.why: Factorial audit shows the system-prompt date is an uncontrolled hidden variable that flips 6.6% of test items and can reduce held-out accuracy by 36.5 points.
highlights.key_result: Across six instruction-tuned models and four benchmarks, two plausible dates (2024--2026) switch a median 6.6% of test items between correct and incorrect, and optimized dates cost the Llama-3.x models up to 36.5 points of held-out accuracy.
evidence: Across six instruction-tuned models and four benchmarks, with prompts, decoding, and configuration fixed, every model is affected: two plausible dates (2024--2026) switch a median 6.6% of test items between correct and incorrect.
In addition, using a grammar-constrained variant of Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) to search dates of any year, we find dates that cost the Llama-3.x models up to 36.5 points of held-out accuracy.

highlights.title: Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability
highlights.authors: Fazl Barez, Tung-Yu Wu, Ivan Arcuschin et al.
highlights.why: Positions chain-of-thought as not explainability, synthesizing evidence of unfaithfulness and finding 21.7% of recent CoT papers treat it as load-bearing interpretability.
highlights.key_result: The paper systematically shows that verbalised chains are frequently unfaithful, diverging from the critical hidden computations that drive a model's predictions. Its analysis of 1,000 recent CoT-centric papers finds that approximately 21.7% explicitly treat CoT as a load-bearing interpretability technique, with higher adoption in high-stakes domains: 40% of medical AI papers (14/35), 38% of autonomous systems papers (14/37), and 23% of papers in law and finance (3/13) make this claim.
evidence: By synthesising evidence from prior work, we systematically show that verbalised chains are frequently unfaithful, diverging from the critical hidden computations that drive a model's predictions.

As CoT is increasingly relied upon in application domains, including high-stakes ones such as medicine, law, and autonomous systems, we further argue that this unfaithfulness is not taken seriously enough in these settings: our analysis of 1,000 recent CoT-centric papers finds that approximately 21.7% explicitly treat CoT as a load-bearing interpretability technique, building pipelines or safety arguments that would not hold if CoT is unfaithful to the model's actual reasoning.

The adoption of this interpretability claim is notably higher in high-stakes domains: 40% of medical AI papers (14/35), 38% of autonomous systems papers (14/37), and 23% of papers in law and finance (3/13) make this claim.

highlights.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
highlights.why: Weakest-link analysis shows per-attack blocking hides catalog vulnerability, which rises from 22% to 99% as tools grow from 10 to 200 despite stable per-attack rates.
highlights.key_result: In two engines, an 8% source-budget error rate leaves per-attack blocking near 92% while the tests find a hole in 99.4% of independently authored 200-tool catalogs, and the error budget falls as 1/M. Correlated authoring lowers that risk without changing per-attack blocking, and on real tools the models' own manifests leave 9 of 15 catalogs open at 89% per-attack blocking.

highlights.title: Medical Image Segmentation Is Now Just Another Coding Task
highlights.authors: Shuheng Cao, Ruiqi Chen, Qizhen Lan et al.
highlights.theme: Medical multimodal foundation models and segmentation
highlights.why: Shows off-the-shelf coding agents can build medical image segmenters reaching 99% of GPU-trained nnU-Net Dice on nine 2D tasks and surpass it with feedback.
highlights.key_result: Given only a task description, labeled data, and a CPU---with no segmentation framework, no pretrained weights, and no human in the loop---four off-the-shelf coding agents built segmenters for 13 tasks across four imaging modalities within hours, an ability that has emerged rather than been built. On the nine 2D tasks, their best programs reach 99% of the Dice of a GPU-trained nnU-Net.

On the nine 2D tasks, their best programs reach 99% of the Dice of a GPU-trained nnU-Net.

highlights.title: BODYBENCH: Evaluating Adversarial Image Defenses Against AI Nudification Inpainting
highlights.authors: Li Qiwei, Salma Abdel Magid, Olga Russakovsky et al.
highlights.why: Reformulates adversarial image protection around nudification inpainting and finds four recent defenses almost entirely fail under harm-aligned metrics.
highlights.key_result: Auditing four recent protection methods (PhotoGuard, DiffusionGuard, AdvPaint, DiffVax) on BodyBench, the paper finds that protection succeeds in only one configuration of one method, and only under exact mask alignment between defender and attacker: only AdvPaint reaches a DefenseScore of 0.951. PSNR and SSIM are essentially uncorrelated with nudity (r=-0.16 and r=-0.18).
evidence: Auditing four recent protection methods (PhotoGuard, DiffusionGuard, AdvPaint, DiffVax) on BodyBench, we find that protection succeeds in only one configuration of one method, and only under exact mask alignment between defender and attacker---a condition no real defender can guarantee and one that we show is easily always bypassed.
Only AdvPaint reaches a DefenseScore of 0.951, and only when the defender's protection mask exactly matches the attacker's mask, requiring the defender to know the attack in advance.

PSNR and SSIM are computed between the protected attacked image and the corresponding unprotected attacked image from the same base image and attack mask. Both have near-zero correlation with DefenseScore (r=-0.16) and (r=-0.18), indicating that pixel-level similarity is not informative of defense success.

highlights.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
highlights.authors: Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Shicheng Cao et al.
highlights.why: Scales a fast world action model to five-minute context and large robot/egocentric pretraining, matching imagine-then-act while decoding actions in 60 ms.
highlights.key_result: Direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6 faster than IDM). G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging.
evidence: Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6 faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging.

highlights.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
highlights.theme: LLM benchmark validity and evaluation bias
highlights.why: Proposes LLM-judge scoring of Spec-Test Coverage Gap to detect overspecified SWE-bench-style tests, validating that they can shift leaderboards after regrading failed patches.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows overspecified tests are detectable and common: the judges flag 89% of known-overspecified tasks and only 4% of known-fine tasks, and flag 23% of Verified and 35% of Pro tasks; on Verified, the top 30 submissions resolve only 31% of flagged tasks on average, against 88% of the other tasks. Relaxing the tests lets 61% of the 2,186 failed patches on flagged tasks pass.
evidence: (1) Overspecified tests are detectable: on the validation tasks, the judges correctly flag 89% of the tasks that human audits identify as overspecified and wrongly flag only 4% of the tasks known to be fine. (2) Overspecified tests are common: applied to whole benchmarks, the judges flag 23% of Verified and 35% of Pro tasks. (3) Flagged tasks are much harder for agents: the top 30 Verified submissions resolve only 31% of the flagged tasks on average, against 88% of the other tasks. (4) Overspecified tests change the leaderboard: relaxing the tests lets 61% of the 2,186 failed patches on flagged tasks pass.

news.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
news.summary: OpenAI reports in a preprint titled "GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models" that its GPT-6 family can design protein structures and amino acid sequences using only reasoning and coding tools, without calling specialized biology models. In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT-6.2's designs showed evidence of binding across five targets, and an internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many of the 14 protein tasks tested.

news.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra
news.summary: Two amateur astronomers, Kevin Bond and Ethan Byrd, used OpenAI's Codex and Astra to search public telescope data for exoplanet transits; Bond scanned about 100,000 Kepler stars and flagged more than 200 signals, including 10 from previously confirmed planets, while Byrd analyzed data from about 19 million stars. An independent SETI Institute search found two of the same signals in the Kepler data, and one of Byrd's candidates was sent to TESS researchers for further analysis.

news.title: How Gemini is changing the game for Golden State's organization and fans.
news.summary: Google expanded its partnership with Golden State, making Gemini the Official AI Assistant Partner and Official Generative AI & Enterprise LLM Partner of the Warriors, the 2026 WNBA Champion Valkyries, and Chase Center. The deal covers interactive videoboard and digital fan features plus internal deployment of Gemini for business to build custom AI agents.

news.title: How to Run NVIDIA Cosmos 3 on Local AI Devices Using Hugging Face Diffusers
news.summary: NVIDIA published a tutorial for running Cosmos 3 Nano, a world foundation model that generates video from text, images and other inputs, on GPUs with as little as 12 GB of VRAM using Hugging Face Diffusers and a Cosmos-Framework offloading package that keeps weights in system RAM. It cites benchmarks across GeForce RTX 5070, 5080, 4090 and 5090, with the RTX 5070 completing 720p text-to-video in 2,624.9 seconds at 9.94 GiB peak memory using BF16, and an FP8 checkpoint option.

news.title: Prepare Market Data for Forecasting with NVIDIA Megatron Core
news.summary: NVIDIA described a Megatron Core and Megatron-LM preprocessing pipeline that converts intraday market-bar Parquet files into model-ready tensors by grouping bars into patches, sliding fixed-length context windows, and computing return and trading-volume targets across multiple horizons. Saved splits (train.pt, val.pt, test.pt, meta.pt) keep parsing outside the training loop, and date-based splits with embargo periods and per-horizon statistics computed only from the training split guard against leakage.

news.title: What’s New for Game Developers: AI Animation and RTX Tools
news.summary: NVIDIA's game developer update covers Gaijin Entertainment integrating DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering into War Thunder's Dagor Engine, and NVIDIA Kimodo becoming the first AI motion-generation model in Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview's guided animation framework, generating character motion from text prompts, spline paths and target poses. It also lists In-Game Inferencing SDK 1.8, RTX Dynamic Illumination 3.2, Real-Time BVH Viewer 1.0 and RTX Path Tracing 1.9 updates.

news.title: Q&A: How Everstone Brings Where Winds Meet to Life with NVIDIA DLSS 5
news.summary: In a Q&A, Everstone Studio art director Muzi Li and engine tech lead Cory Zhou described integrating NVIDIA DLSS 5 into Where Winds Meet via their existing Streamline integration, using model selection and structural and tonal strength controls. They said Jiangnan shows the largest gains and that internal testing indicates additional performance overhead, so players will be able to enable or disable DLSS 5.

news.title: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton
news.summary: A Hugging Face tutorial adds local obstacle avoidance to the Microduck robot while keeping its walking policy frozen, training a separate controller in NVIDIA Isaac Lab that uses Newton-simulated time-of-flight depth sensing to adjust gamepad velocity commands at 50 Hz. Courses are built from SimReady assets such as a cardboard box, office bin, bedside cabinet and cones, with layouts resampled at each episode reset.

news.title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API, with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls for Claude models
news.summary: AWS announced general availability of the trusted access program API on Amazon Bedrock, a single place to discover, request and enroll in model provider trusted access programs, plus public preview of two Claude offerings built with Anthropic: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC). With EFS, customer data stays in their own AWS account and prompts and completions are not retained by Anthropic or Amazon Bedrock; with EDC, retained data is stored in Amazon-managed storage.

highlights.authors: Shuheng Cao, Ruiqi Chen, Qizhen Lan et al.
highlights.theme: Medical multimodal foundation models and segmentation
highlights.why: 表明现成的编码智能体可以构建医学图像分割器，在九个2D任务上达到GPU训练的nnU-Net的Dice值的99%，并且在反馈下可以超越它。
highlights.key_result: 仅给定任务描述、标注数据和CPU——没有分割框架、没有预训练权重、也没有人类参与——四个现成的编码智能体在数小时内为四种成像模态下的13个任务构建了分割器，这种能力是涌现出来而非构建出来的。在九个2D任务上，它们的最佳程序达到了GPU训练的nnU-Net的Dice值的99%。
evidence: Given only a task description, labeled data, and a CPU---with no segmentation framework, no pretrained weights, and no human in the loop---four off-the-shelf coding agents built segmenters for 13 tasks across four imaging modalities within hours, an ability that has emerged rather than been built. On the nine 2D tasks, their best programs reach 99% of the Dice of a GPU-trained nnU-Net.

highlights.title: BODYBENCH: Evaluating Adversarial Image Defenses Against AI Nudification Inpainting
highlights.authors: Li Qiwei, Salma Abdel Magid, Olga Russakovsky et al.
highlights.why: 围绕裸露图像修复重新表述了对抗性图像保护，并发现四种近期防御在伤害对齐指标下几乎完全失效。
highlights.key_result: 在BodyBench上审计四种近期保护方法（PhotoGuard、DiffusionGuard、AdvPaint、DiffVax），论文发现保护仅在一种方法的一种配置下成功，并且仅在防御者和攻击者之间精确掩码对齐时：只有AdvPaint达到了0.951的DefenseScore。PSNR和SSIM与裸露程度基本不相关（r=-0.16和r=-0.18）。
evidence: Auditing four recent protection methods (PhotoGuard, DiffusionGuard, AdvPaint, DiffVax) on BodyBench, we find that protection succeeds in only one configuration of one method, and only under exact mask alignment between defender and attacker---a condition no real defender can guarantee and one that we show is easily always bypassed.
Only AdvPaint reaches a DefenseScore of 0.951, and only when the defender's protection mask exactly matches the attacker's mask, requiring the defender to know the attack in advance.

PSNR and SSIM are computed between the protected attacked image and the corresponding unprotected attacked image from the same base image and attack mask. Both have near-zero correlation with DefenseScore (r=-0.16) and (r=-0.18), indicating that pixel-level similarity is not informative of defense success.

highlights.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
highlights.authors: Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Shicheng Cao et al.
highlights.why: 将快速世界动作模型扩展到五分钟上下文和大规模机器人/自我中心预训练，在60毫秒内解码动作的同时匹配先想象后行动。
highlights.key_result: 直接动作解码（Fast模式）与相同检查点的先想象后行动（IDM）推理效果相当，同时在单个RTX 5090上每个16步动作块运行60毫秒（比IDM快7.6倍）。G0.7在五个仿真基准套件上取得70.8的平均分，在Galaxea R1 Pro和R1 Lite上分别获得48%和54%的零样本抓取放置成功率，在视频条件化的上下文学习任务上获得96.7%的分布内成功率和93.3%的分布外成功率，在七个真实世界后训练任务（包括数分钟的折盒子、准备饮料和产品装袋）中取得86.9%的平均任务进度。
evidence: Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6 faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging.

highlights.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
highlights.theme: LLM benchmark validity and evaluation bias
highlights.why: 提出使用LLM评判器对Spec-Test Coverage Gap进行评分，以检测过度指定的SWE-bench风格测试，并验证在重新评分失败补丁后它们可以改变排行榜。
highlights.key_result: 论文表明过度指定的测试是可检测且常见的：评判器标记了89%已知过度指定的任务，仅标记了4%已知正常的任务，并标记了23%的Verified任务和35%的Pro任务；在Verified上，前30个提交平均仅解决了31%的标记任务，而其他任务为88%。放宽测试后，标记任务上2,186个失败补丁中有61%可以通过。
evidence: (1) Overspecified tests are detectable: on the validation tasks, the judges correctly flag 89% of the tasks that human audits identify as overspecified and wrongly flag only 4% of the tasks known to be fine. (2) Overspecified tests are common: applied to whole benchmarks, the judges flag 23% of Verified and 35% of Pro tasks. (3) Flagged tasks are much harder for agents: the top 30 Verified submissions resolve only 31% of the flagged tasks on average, against 88% of the other tasks. (4) Overspecified tests change the leaderboard: relaxing the tests lets 61% of the 2,186 failed patches on flagged tasks pass.

news.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
news.summary: OpenAI在一篇题为“GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models”的预印本中报告称，其GPT-6系列仅使用推理和编码工具就能设计蛋白质结构和氨基酸序列，而无需调用专门的生物学模型。在与Onava的实验室测试中，基于GPT-6.2设计的蛋白质在五个靶点上显示出结合证据，而且一个内部研究模型在许多测试的14个蛋白质任务中达到或超过了专门模型。

news.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra
news.summary: 两位业余天文学家Kevin Bond和Ethan Byrd使用OpenAI的Codex和Astra搜索公共望远镜数据以寻找系外行星凌星；Bond扫描了约100,000颗开普勒恒星并标记了200多个信号，其中10个来自先前确认的行星，而Byrd分析了约19 million颗恒星的数据。SETI研究所的一项独立搜索在开普勒数据中发现了两个相同的信号，Byrd的一个候选信号被发送给TESS研究人员进行进一步分析。

news.title: How Gemini is changing the game for Golden State's organization and fans.
news.summary: Google扩大了与Golden State的合作，使Gemini成为勇士队、2026年WNBA冠军Valkyries队以及Chase Center的官方AI助手合作伙伴和官方生成式AI与企业LLM合作伙伴。该协议涵盖交互式视频板和数字球迷功能，以及在内部部署Gemini for business以构建定制AI智能体。

news.title: How to Run NVIDIA Cosmos 3 on Local AI Devices Using Hugging Face Diffusers
news.summary: NVIDIA发布了一篇教程，介绍如何在显存低至12 GB的GPU上运行Cosmos 3 Nano（一个世界基础模型，可从文本、图像和其他输入生成视频），使用Hugging Face Diffusers和一个Cosmos-Framework卸载包将权重保存在系统RAM中。该教程引用了GeForce RTX 5070、5080、4090和5090的基准测试，其中RTX 5070使用BF16在9.94 GiB峰值内存下以2,624.9秒完成720p文本到视频，并提供了FP8检查点选项。

news.title: Prepare Market Data for Forecasting with NVIDIA Megatron Core
news.summary: NVIDIA描述了一个Megatron Core和Megatron-LM预处理流水线，该流水线通过将柱状数据分组为patch、滑动固定长度的上下文窗口以及计算多个时间范围的收益和交易量目标，将日内市场柱Parquet文件转换为模型就绪的张量。保存的划分（train.pt、val.pt、test.pt、meta.pt）将解析保持在训练循环之外，基于日期的划分带有禁运期，并且每个时间范围的统计量仅从训练划分计算，以防止泄漏。

news.title: What’s New for Game Developers: AI Animation and RTX Tools
news.summary: NVIDIA的游戏开发者更新涵盖Gaijin Entertainment将DLSS 5与3D-Guided Neural Rendering集成到War Thunder的Dagor引擎中，以及NVIDIA Kimodo成为Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview引导动画框架中的第一个AI动作生成模型，可从文本提示、样条路径和目标姿态生成角色动作。它还列出了In-Game Inferencing SDK 1.8、RTX Dynamic Illumination 3.2、Real-Time BVH Viewer 1.0和RTX Path Tracing 1.9的更新。

news.title: Q&A: How Everstone Brings Where Winds Meet to Life with NVIDIA DLSS 5
news.summary: 在一次问答中，Everstone Studio艺术总监Muzi Li和引擎技术负责人Cory Zhou描述了通过他们现有的Streamline集成将NVIDIA DLSS 5集成到《燕云十六声》中，使用模型选择以及结构和色调强度控制。他们表示江南地区显示出最大的提升，内部测试表明存在额外的性能开销，因此玩家将能够启用或禁用DLSS 5。

news.title: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton
news.summary: Hugging Face教程为Microduck机器人添加了局部避障功能，同时保持其行走策略不变，在NVIDIA Isaac Lab中训练一个单独的控制器，该控制器使用Newton模拟的飞行时间深度传感，以50 Hz的频率调整游戏手柄速度命令。赛道由SimReady资产构建，如纸板箱、办公室垃圾桶、床头柜和锥体，布局在每个回合重置时重新采样。

news.title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API, with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls for Claude models
news.summary: AWS宣布Amazon Bedrock上的可信访问计划API正式可用，这是一个发现、请求和注册模型提供商可信访问计划的统一入口，同时还公开预览了两项与Anthropic合作构建的Claude产品：Enterprise Frontier Safeguards（EFS）和Enterprise Data Controls（EDC）。使用EFS时，客户数据保留在他们自己的AWS账户中，提示和补全不会被Anthropic或Amazon Bedrock保留；使用EDC时，保留的数据存储在Amazon托管的存储中。
